text:
The court will most likely choose **B**: the defendant's bare testimony that he kept the records regularly does not establish the trustworthiness of the computer-generated data, so a greater foundation is required. Option A states only one element of the business-records exception, and the other elements, such as entries made by someone with knowledge at or near the time, are not shown. The team note is wrong: a declarant's availability to testify does not take an out-of-court statement outside the hearsay rule, so C fails, and no reliability of the computer process has been shown, so D fails.

CONFIDENCE: 72
